dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, filter.json, utils.py; sampled all three suites; identified wacc as Nora Sandler book progression, characterized feature distribution (structs/bitfields/switch/preprocessor) and used it to scope priorities before writing code.

Ran full harness to learn per-suite pass/fail scoring, obtained breakdown (c_testsuite 134/146, wacc 214/221, gcc 276/413), then targeted specific failures — confirms understanding of how tests are judged.
Verified ABI/assembler reality by generating gcc's own assembly and testing it against `as` to find why `cx[rip]` failed — ground-truth verification rather than assumption.
Reasoned explicitly about SysV details: int→long argument conversion at call sites and struct-by-value passing rules (<=16 bytes in regs vs stack).

Sustained late-horizon drilling into exact C constructs (bitfield sign, designated-init zeroing with byte-offset analysis, case ranges, nested struct tags), treating suites as an evolving spec to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized the corpus and scoring mechanism up front (anchor 8), verified ABI and assembler behavior against actual gcc output rather than recall (anchor 8), and sustained fine-grained investigation of specific failing C constructs and their reference behavior across the entire trajectory, feeding findings back into design (anchor 10). It falls just short of a clean 10 because some ABI corners (struct-by-value) were deferred rather than fully modeled, placing it at a strong 9.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Explored test suites and wacc chapter progression to understand feature scope; explicitly stated 'build a minimal working compiler that handles the simplest tests first, then extend' — showing stage awareness.

Contradicted that intent by deciding to 'Write a comprehensive C compiler in one shot,' writing lexer/preprocess/parser/sema/codegen all at once. No dependency-ordered milestone sequence; foundational and dependent features built together.
First full-suite run gave 80%; agent then worked failure-to-failure, picking specific failing test IDs to fix rather than following any pre-planned milestone order.

Fix loop consistently used concrete per-item done-signals (individual test passes) plus full-suite re-runs to track pass counts, but grouped fixes ad hoc by category (structs, bitfields, floats) with no explicit milestone plan naming feature→pipeline→certifying tests.
Ending confirms pattern: tracked 747/780=95.8% and hunted 'quick easy wins,' never returning to a structured milestone hierarchy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent recognized scope and did track progress against test subsets and pass counts throughout the long fix loop, using concrete individual-test done-signals — which lifts it above the level-3 'rough mental list with no per-milestone check.' But it did NOT build in dependency-ordered stages (it wrote the whole compiler in one shot, closer to the level-0 'whole language at once' tendency) and never maintained an explicit ordered milestone plan tying features to pipeline changes and certifying tests, so it falls short of level 5's genuine 'work in sensible stages, layering features.' This mix places it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Repeatedly wrote minimal C repros (echo/cat > /tmp/x.c) to isolate a struct-scope bug, register-name-collision bug, and long-long call bug, progressively narrowing to the failing construct.
Inspected emitted assembly via -S flag against expected instructions, catching concrete codegen bugs like wrong load vs lea, and mixed-size 'and eax,rax'/missing r10 in sized_reg.
Bisected to single instructions and confirmed edge semantics: test rax vs eax, shift promotion, unary-minus integer promotion, cast sign-extension — validating each fix at the right granularity.
Built targeted bitfield repros checking layout sizes, then read/write/compound-assign/init, verifying runtime output before scaling to full suite.

Categorized remaining failures by root cause (bitfields, floats, vectors, struct-by-value) to prioritize, using full-suite pass counts (91.7%→95.8%) as coarse progress gauge between fine-grained fixes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently engineered a verification loop far tighter than the 780-test harness: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, -S assembly inspection, per-feature slices, and dual compile+runtime checks — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It exceeds 8 in places by confirming edge semantics (promotion, alignment, sign-extension, overflow) and categorizing failures by root cause, but stops short of level 10 because verification stayed ad-hoc (one-off repros, manual bisection, grep on asm) rather than reusable harnesses or systematic asm-diffing against gcc.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: On first full test run, immediately records per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 134/146, wacc 214/221, gcc_torture 276/413), establishing a structured pass/fail-by-suite picture rather than a bare aggregate.
Maintains /tmp/failures.txt ledger and at step 99 diffs new failures against the saved prior version to detect what changed ('one tradeoff. Let me see what changed') — explicit regression check.
Flags a suspected regression ('00106 is now failing!'), re-runs and investigates until confirming it was stale state, not a real backslide — active regression vigilance.
Uses failure counts to allocate effort to highest-yield work: targets bitfield tests because '4 use them' and struct-by-value because it 'affects multiple tests.'
Tracks a running pass-rate trend after nearly every change (91.7%→92.9%→...→95.8%), using it to gauge net progress across the horizon.
Detects stall near the end ('Stable at 747/780 = 95.8%') and correctly recognizes remaining failures require out-of-scope features, avoiding wasted circular effort.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by suite, tracks an aggregate trend after each significant change, maintains a failures ledger it diffs to catch regressions, investigates suspected backslides, and uses the trend to target the highest-yield failures — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the regression-diffing was intermittent rather than performed systematically after every change, and later tracking relied mostly on the aggregate percentage instead of a persistent per-category newly-passing/newly-broken ledger.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Global name 'cx' collided with a register name in Intel syntax. The agent explicitly weighed a full AT&T-syntax rewrite ('HUGE rewrite') against a surgical symbol-mangling fix, diagnosed the true root cause (gas parsing register-name-like symbols), and chose the targeted redesign with clear trade-off reasoning — classic level-8 behavior.

Function name 'not' hit the same class of assembler-collision bug; the agent generalized its mangling scheme to all defined functions while deliberately preserving extern/stdlib names — recognizing a recurring root cause rather than one-off patching.

Diagnosed that argument passing and compound-assignment both mishandled type sizes/common-type promotion (a cluster of sized-operation failures) and rewrote gen_call and the compound-assign path rather than band-aiding individual tests.

Root-caused an intermittent/flaky failure to HashMap iteration nondeterminism in struct layout ordering — distinguished a real structural nondeterminism bug from a spurious test result and fixed the ordering.

Recognized bitfields were entirely unsupported in codegen (not just buggy), then built out layout fix + extract/insert helpers + compound-assign + init handling as a cohesive subsystem, judging it worthwhile for ~4 tests.

Repeatedly made conscious NON-redesign decisions (struct scoping 'first-wins', deferring float/xmm, struct-by-value, vectors) with explicit scope/trade-off reasoning — avoiding needless churn, but also leaving the float foundation (a known recurring gap) unaddressed, which caps it below the anticipatory level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures (symbol-name collisions, sized-op/promotion bugs, HashMap nondeterminism), distinguishes local bugs from structural limitations, and undertakes targeted redesigns (symbol mangling, gen_call/compound-assign rewrites, bitfield subsystem) with explicit trade-off reasoning — squarely matching the level-8 description. It falls short of 10 because it is largely reactive rather than anticipatory and consciously defers a known structural gap (float/xmm codegen) instead of pivoting to fix the foundation; combined with a fair amount of symptom-level sed patching between the bigger refactors, this lands at a strong 7.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Explicit up-front decomposition into lexer/preprocess/parser/sema/codegen modules with an AST and a struct/enum layout table — a coherent staged pipeline (anchor 5 baseline).
Deliberate, explicitly-reasoned decision to keep sema thin and push type computation into codegen. Rationale was made explicit, but this choice limited extensibility of type-aware codegen.
Separate gen_lval lvalue-vs-rvalue path — a deliberate hard-part representation choice, and struct-layout bitfield offsets designed into sema (288-303), pushing above a bare 5.

C usual-arithmetic-conversion behavior (arg casts, conditional common type, compound-assign, shift, unary-neg promotion) was retrofitted via individual codegen patches rather than a general typed-value conversion mechanism — escalating special-casing, the opposite of anchor 8's 'slot in with minimal disruption'.
Symbol/struct scoping never designed: global 'first-wins' tag registry, with proper lexical scoping repeatedly deferred as 'non-trivial, skip' — a representational gap in the scope model.

Struct layout representation relied on HashMap iteration order, producing nondeterministic layout failures that had to be diagnosed and fixed — evidence the aggregate-layout representation wasn't fully robust by design.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent committed up front to a genuinely coherent staged pipeline (distinct lexer/preprocessor/parser/sema/codegen, AST, struct layout table) and made some deliberate hard-part representation choices — separate lvalue/rvalue paths and bitfield-aware struct layout — which lifts it above anchor 5. But it does not reach anchor 8: a central design decision to put type computation in codegen forced C's arithmetic conversions to be handled by escalating per-feature special-casing rather than a general typed-value abstraction, and symbol/struct scoping was never designed (global first-wins tags, scoping repeatedly skipped). Breadth was absorbed partly by design and partly by special-casing, placing it at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
